sounds.name: Expressive Lead #1
sounds.ref: From the Behringer System 35 guide
sounds.blurb: Three sawtooth oscillators through the ladder filter, with a vibrato that fades in on held notes through the CP3A-O.
sounds.how: The guide’s first lead on the System 35. Three 921Bs chained from one 921A are mixed into the 904A, with one 911 on the amplifier and another on the cutoff. The vibrato comes from the 921 through the second 902, which the third 911 opens slowly; the CP3A-O then sends it, through its attenuator, to all three oscillators’ DC MOD inputs at once. Switch it in and out with the CP3A-O’s rocker 4.

steps.title: Three linked oscillators
steps.why:
The keyboard drives the first 921A, and its three 921Bs are chained from it, two of them slightly detuned.
- Cables: CM1A CV 1 to 921A (1) FREQUENCY IN 1; 921A (1) to 921B (1); 921B (1) on to 921B (2), and 921B (2) on to 921B (3).
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY +0.08, 921B (3) FREQUENCY −0.1.

steps.title: Mixer, filter, amplifier, envelopes
steps.why:
All three SAWTOOTH outputs into the first CP3A-M, then the 904A and the first 902. The trigger goes through CP35 MULTIPLE A to all three 911s; the first opens the 902, the second sweeps the filter.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1–3 at 5, MASTER 8.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −1, REGENERATION 2.
- 911 (1): T1 3, T2 6, E SUS 8, T3 6. 911 (2): T1 3, T2 6.5, E SUS 4, T3 6.
- Listen for: a big, warm three-oscillator lead.

steps.title: A delayed vibrato through the CP3A-O
steps.why:
The 921 runs slowly into the second 902, which the third 911 opens over about two seconds. The 902’s output goes to the CP3A-O’s EXT INPUT, and the CP3A-O’s three outputs go to the three DC MODs.
- 921 COARSE RNG on SUB, FREQUENCY +1, AUX OUT WAVEFORM sine, AUX OUT LEVEL 10.
- 911 (3): T1 8, T2 5, E SUS 10, T3 4.
- CP3A-O (1) ROUTING SWITCH 4 on, ATTENUATOR 1.2.
- Listen for: hold a note and the vibrato swells in.

context.cp3ao_1.attenuator: In this sound: the vibrato depth for all three oscillators at once.
context.cp3ao_1.route4: In this sound: switches the vibrato in and out without unplugging anything.
context.m911_3.t1: In this sound: how long the vibrato takes to fade in.
context.m921.frequency: In this sound: the vibrato speed.

tweaks.hear: No vibrato at all.

tweaks.try: Turn the CP3A-O ATTENUATOR up to 3
tweaks.hear: A much wider, operatic vibrato.

sounds.name: Expressive Lead #2
sounds.ref: From the Behringer System 35 guide
sounds.blurb: Two pulse waves with moving width, in two layers: the ladder filter, and a thinner band-pass part through the 923.
sounds.how: The guide’s second lead uses both mixers. The first CP3A-M mixes two rectangular waves whose width the slow 921 sweeps through the 921A. Its first output goes to the 904A; its second goes through the 923’s high-pass and then its low-pass, a gentle band-pass. Each layer has its own 902 and 911, and the second CP3A-M mixes them, so you can balance a round lead against a thin, nasal one.

steps.title: Two pulse waves with moving width
steps.why:
Pitch and width from the first 921A to two 921Bs; the 921, through CP35 attenuator 1, sweeps the width.
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY +0.12. 921 COARSE RNG on SUB, FREQUENCY −0.5. CP35 ATTENUATOR 1 at 2.5.
- Cables: the keyboard, frequency and width links; RECTANGULAR (1) and (2) to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 1 and 2; 921 SINE through CP35 attenuator 1 to 921A (1) WIDTH IN 1.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1 and 2 at 6, MASTER 8.

steps.title: The main layer: 904A
steps.why:
CP3A-M (1) OUTPUT + 1 to the 904A, then the first 902 under the first 911, into the second mixer and out.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE 0, REGENERATION 2. 911 (1): T1 2, T2 6, E SUS 8, T3 5.5.
- CP3A-M (2) GAIN 1 at 7, MASTER 8.
- Listen for: a round, reedy lead.

steps.title: A thin layer: the 923 as a band-pass
steps.why:
CP3A-M (1) OUTPUT + 2 through the 923 HIGH PASS and then its LOW PASS, then the second 902 under the second 911.
- 923 HIGH PASS 6 (about 630 Hz), LOW PASS 8 (about 2.5 kHz).
- 911 (2): T1 4, T2 6.5, E SUS 6, T3 6. CP3A-M (2) GAIN 2 at 5.
- Listen for: a nasal edge on top of the lead. Balance the two with the second mixer’s GAIN 1 and 2.

context.m923.hp: In this sound: the bottom of the band-pass layer.
context.m923.lp: In this sound: the top of the band-pass layer.
context.cp35.att1: In this sound: how far the pulse width sweeps.

tweaks.hear: Only the thin, nasal band-pass layer is left.

tweaks.try: Turn T1 on the second 911 up to 7
tweaks.hear: The nasal layer swells in behind each note.

sounds.name: Mellow Organ
sounds.ref: From the Behringer System 35 guide
sounds.blurb: Three oscillators through the 914 for the organ tone, plus a tuned click and a noise click for the key attack.
sounds.how: The guide builds an organ from three parts, each with its own 902 and 911, mixed in the second CP3A-M. The tone is a triangle, a square and a sine from three 921Bs, shaped by the 914 with only a few low bands up. The fourth 921B, on the second 921A, gives a sine pinged through the 904A with a 500 ms decay: a tuned “tock” at the start of each note. Pink noise through the 904B with a 5 ms decay adds the key click.

steps.title: The organ tone through the 914
steps.why:
CM1A CV 1 goes through CP35 MULTIPLE B to both 921As. The first drives three 921Bs: TRIANGLE (1), RECTANGULAR (2) and SINE (3) into the first mixer, then the 914, the first 902 and the second mixer.
- 914: 125 and 175 at 4, 350 at 5, 500 at 3.5, 1400 at 1, everything else 0.
- 921A (1) WIDTH 5 (50 %).
- 911 (1): T1 0, T2 10, E SUS 10, T3 0: on while the key is held, like an organ.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1–3 at 6, MASTER 10. CP3A-M (2) GAIN 1 at 8, MASTER 8.

steps.title: A tuned click
steps.why:
The second 921A drives the fourth 921B, whose SINE goes through the 904A and the second 902. The second 911 has no sustain, so each note gets a short, tuned “tock”.
- 911 (2): T1 0, T2 6.5 (500 ms), E SUS 0, T3 0.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE 3.
- CP3A-M (2) GAIN 2 at 5.

steps.title: A noise click
steps.why:
Pink noise through the 904B and the third 902, with a 5 ms envelope: the key click, kept low in the mix.
- 911 (3): T1 0, T2 1.1 (5 ms), E SUS 0, T3 0.
- 904B FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE 2. CP3A-M (2) GAIN 3 at 3.
- Listen for: a little “tick” at the start of each note.

context.m914.band_350: In this sound: the main body of the organ tone.
context.cp3am_2.gain2: In this sound: how loud the tuned “tock” is.
context.cp3am_2.gain3: In this sound: how loud the noise click is.
context.m921a_1.width: In this sound: above 5 the square wave narrows and the organ gets more nasal.

tweaks.try: Turn the first 921A’s WIDTH up to 8
tweaks.hear: A thinner, more nasal reed organ.
A brighter, more cutting organ.

sounds.name: Percussive Lead
sounds.ref: From the Behringer System 35 guide
sounds.blurb: A triangle and a detuned sawtooth with a hard front and a slowly moving filter, made for fast lines.
sounds.how: The same patch as on the System 15. The first 911 gives the amplifier an instant attack and a short fall to a low sustain; the second opens the filter slowly and lets it go over seconds, and the 921 sways it on top.

steps.title: Triangle, sawtooth and a hard front
steps.why:
TRIANGLE (1) and SAWTOOTH (2) mixed into the 904A and the first 902 under the first 911.
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY +0.08. CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1 at 7, GAIN 2 at 5, MASTER 8.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −1, REGENERATION 3.
- 911 (1): T1 0, T2 5.4, E SUS 4, T3 5.4.

steps.title: Slow filter movement
steps.why:
The second 911 opens the filter slowly; the 921, through CP35 attenuator 1, sways it.
- 911 (2): T1 7.3, T2 3.8, E SUS 9, T3 8.9. 921 on SUB, FREQUENCY −1. CP35 ATTENUATOR 1 at 1.5.
- Listen for: the line brightens the longer you play.

context.m911_1.esus: In this sound: how much of each note is left after the hard front.
context.m911_2.t1: In this sound: how slowly the filter opens.

tweaks.try: Turn E SUS on the first 911 down to 0
tweaks.hear: Every note becomes a short pluck.

sounds.name: Space Rock
sounds.ref: From the Behringer System 35 guide
sounds.blurb: A whistling self-oscillating filter swept by two slow oscillators, over wind from pink noise.
sounds.how: The 904A with REGENERATION near the top rings on its own, and the 921 and the first 921B (on LO) move its pitch. Pink noise through the 904B, swept by the second 921B, is the wind. Neither needs the keyboard.

steps.title: The singing filter, swept
steps.why:
The 904A rings at REGENERATION 9.5, FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −2; the 921 and the first 921B on LO sweep it.
- 921 on SUB, FREQUENCY −2. 921B (1) RANGE LO; 921A (1) FREQUENCY −6 on OCTAVE.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1 at 9, MASTER 9.
- Cables: 921 SINE and 921B (1) SINE to 904A CONTROL INPUTS 1 and 2; 904A to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 1; CP3A-M to OUTPUT.

steps.title: Wind
steps.why:
Pink noise through the 904B, swept by the second 921B on LO.
- 921B (2) RANGE LO, FREQUENCY +5. 904B FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE 1. CP3A-M (1) GAIN 2 at 6.

context.m904a.regeneration: In this sound: at 9.5 the filter is the sound source.

tweaks.try: Turn the 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE up to 3
tweaks.hear: A shrill, piercing whistle.

sounds.name: Four-Oscillator Bass
sounds.ref: Two 921A banks under one keyboard
sounds.blurb: Both oscillator banks on one note, an octave apart and detuned, through the ladder filter: a huge, moving bass.
sounds.how: The System 35 has two 921A drivers, each with two 921Bs. With the keyboard sent to both through a multiple, one bank plays at pitch and the other an octave down, each pair slightly detuned against itself, so four sawtooths beat slowly against each other. A snappy filter envelope and key tracking keep it tight.

steps.title: Two banks from one keyboard
steps.why:
CM1A CV 1 into CP35 MULTIPLE B, then to both 921As. Bank 1 at 8’, bank 2 at 16’, each pair detuned.
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY +0.1, 921B (3) RANGE 16’, 921B (4) RANGE 16’, FREQUENCY −0.1.
- All four SAWTOOTHs into the first CP3A-M at GAIN 4, MASTER 8.
- Cables: the keyboard through MULTIPLE B to both 921As; each 921A to its pair of 921Bs; the four SAWTOOTHs to INPUTs 1–4; CP3A-M (1) to 904A to 902 (1) to OUTPUT.

steps.title: Snap and track
steps.why:
The first 911 opens the amplifier, the second snaps the filter, and CM1A CV 2 tracks it.
- 911 (1): T1 0, T2 6, E SUS 8, T3 4. 911 (2): T1 0, T2 5.2, E SUS 2, T3 4.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −0.5, REGENERATION 2.5.
- Cables: triggers to both 911s; 911 (1) to 902 (1); 911 (2) to 904A CONTROL INPUT 1; CM1A CV 2 to 904A CONTROL INPUT 2.

context.m921b_2.frequency: In this sound: the beating within the first pair.
context.m921b_4.frequency: In this sound: the beating within the second pair, an octave down.
context.m911_2.t2: In this sound: the length of the filter snap.

tweaks.hear: The octave below thins out to a single detuned voice.
A rubbery, resonant bass.

sounds.name: Switch the Sweep
sounds.ref: The 992 Control Voltages
sounds.blurb: An envelope, an LFO and the keyboard all patched to the 992, so the rockers choose what moves the filter.
sounds.how: The 992 adds up to three control voltages and an attenuated fourth, and each has its own switch. Here the filter envelope, the 921 LFO and the keyboard CV are all patched in, so you can change how the filter moves by flicking rockers instead of re-patching. The EXT INPUT’s attenuator goes both ways: turned anticlockwise it turns its signal upside down.

steps.title: A voice with the filter on the 992
steps.why:
Two sawtooths through the 904A and the first 902 under the first 911. The 992’s first output goes to the 904A’s CONTROL INPUT 1.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1 and 2 at 6, MASTER 8. 921B (2) FREQUENCY +0.1.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −2, REGENERATION 5.
- 911 (1): T1 2, T2 6, E SUS 8, T3 5.

steps.title: Three sources, three switches
steps.why:
The second 911 into 992 CONTROL INPUT 1, the 921 (through CP35 attenuator 1) into INPUT 2, and CM1A CV 2 into INPUT 3.
- 911 (2): T1 0, T2 5.5, E SUS 2, T3 5. 921 on SUB, FREQUENCY 0. CP35 ATTENUATOR 1 at 2.
- 992 CV SWITCH 1 on, SWITCH 2 off, SWITCH 3 on.
- Listen for: an envelope sweep that tracks the keys. Flick SWITCH 2 on to add a wobble, SWITCH 1 off to lose the sweep.

steps.title: An upside-down envelope
steps.why:
The third 911 into the 992’s EXT INPUT, with the attenuator turned anticlockwise, so it pulls the filter down on each note while the second envelope pushes it up.
- 911 (3): T1 6, T2 7, E SUS 0, T3 6.
- 992 CV SWITCH 4 on, ATTENUATOR −5.
- Cable: CP35 MULTIPLE A 3 to 911 (3) S-TRIG IN; 911 (3) OUT to 992 EXT INPUT.
- Listen for: each note opens, then closes down further than it started before settling.

context.m992.switch1: In this sound: the filter envelope on or off.
context.m992.switch2: In this sound: the LFO wobble on or off.
context.m992.switch3: In this sound: key tracking on or off.
context.m992.attenuator: In this sound: anticlockwise, so the third envelope pulls the filter down.

tweaks.hear: The 921 wobbles the filter on top of the sweep.
The third envelope now pushes the filter up too: a longer, brighter sweep.

sounds.name: Four-Oscillator Lead
sounds.ref: Every oscillator on one note
sounds.blurb: Four oscillators in fifths and octaves, all from the keyboard, for a huge, organ-like lead.
sounds.how: Two banks of two oscillators: the first bank on the note and a fifth above, the second an octave below and an octave above. Played together they reinforce the harmonics of the note, the way an organ’s stops do. The filter envelope opens a little slowly, so each note blooms.

steps.title: Root, fifth and octaves
steps.why:
The keyboard through CP35 MULTIPLE B to both 921As. 921B (2) a fifth up; 921B (3) at 16’, 921B (4) at 4’.
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY +7. 921B (3) RANGE 16’, 921B (4) RANGE 4’, FREQUENCY +0.06.
- SAWTOOTH (1), RECTANGULAR (2), SAWTOOTH (3) and TRIANGLE (4) into CP3A-M (1) at GAIN 6, 3, 5 and 3, MASTER 8.

steps.title: A blooming filter
steps.why:
Both envelopes, the filter one a little slower.
- 911 (1): T1 2.5, T2 6, E SUS 9, T3 5.5. 911 (2): T1 5, T2 6.5, E SUS 5, T3 5.5.
- 904A FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −1.5, REGENERATION 1.5.

context.m921b_2.frequency: In this sound: +7, a fifth above. Try +12 for a plain octave.
context.cp3am_1.gain2: In this sound: the level of the fifth.

tweaks.hear: A hollow, quinty organ lead.
All octaves: rounder and less exotic.

sounds.name: Filter Bank Choir
sounds.ref: The 914 as a vocal formant
sounds.blurb: Four detuned oscillators through the 914 set to an “oo”, with slow envelopes: a soft, wordless choir.
sounds.how: Four sawtooths, slightly out of tune with each other, already sound like a group rather than one voice. Through the 914 with its bands set low and narrow (250 to 500 Hz up, a small peak near 2 kHz, the top cut away) they take on a closed “oo” vowel. Slow T1 and T3 on the 902 make it swell and fade like voices.

steps.title: Four detuned voices
steps.why:
All four 921Bs on sawtooth, each a few cents apart, from both banks.
- 921B (2) +0.1, 921B (3) −0.08, 921B (4) +0.18.
- CP3A-M (1) GAIN 1–4 at 4, MASTER 8.

context.m914.band_350: In this sound: the centre of the “oo”.
context.m914.band_2000: In this sound: a small upper peak that makes it sound sung rather than muffled.
context.m911_1.t1: In this sound: how slowly the choir swells in.

tweaks.hear: The vowel opens towards “ah”.
A wider, more out-of-tune chorus.

sounds.name: Italo Gallop Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Alexander Robotnick — “Problèmes d’amour”, Florence, 1983
sounds.blurb: A galloping eighth-and-two-sixteenths bass, a sawtooth with a square an octave below it, from two oscillator banks played as one.
sounds.how: The CP3A-O is a control-voltage mixer whose three outputs carry the same sum, so one keyboard voltage patched into it comes out three times. Two of those copies play the two 921A drivers, and each bank brings one 921B: a sawtooth at 8’ from the first, a square at 16’ from the second. The 904A gets a short bite from the second 911 through a CP35 attenuator.

steps.title: One keyboard voltage, two banks
steps.why:
The keyboard goes into the first CP3A-O, and its first two outputs play the two 921As. The second bank’s 921B is set an octave down.
- 921B (1) RANGE 8’.
- 921B (3) RANGE 16’.
- 921 COARSE RNG SUB: the 921 plays no part in this sound, so it goes back to its LFO range.
- Cables: CM1A CV 1 to CP3A-O (1) CONTROL INPUT 1; CP3A-O (1) OUTPUT 1 to 921A (1) FREQUENCY IN 1; CP3A-O (1) OUTPUT 2 to 921A (2) FREQUENCY IN 1; 921A (1) FREQUENCY TO 921B to 921B (1) LINK FREQ; 921A (2) FREQUENCY TO 921B to 921B (3) LINK FREQ.
- Unplug (Default patch): CM1A CV 1 from 921 FREQUENCY CONTROL INPUT 1; 921 SAWTOOTH from 902 (1) SIG IN +.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the oscillators run, but nothing reaches the output.

steps.title: Saw over square, through the ladder
steps.why:
The first 921B’s SAWTOOTH and the third 921B’s RECTANGULAR (a square with no width link) into the first CP3A-M, then the 904A and the first 902.
- CP3A-M (1): GAIN 1 5, GAIN 2 4, MASTER GAIN 8.
- 904A: FIXED CONTROL VOLTAGE −0.5, REGENERATION 2.5.
- 911 (1): T1 0 · 2 ms, T2 5 · 140 ms, E SUS 6 · 3.3 V, T3 3 · 26 ms.
- Cables: 921B (1) SAWTOOTH to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 1; 921B (3) RECTANGULAR to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 2; CP3A-M (1) OUTPUT + 1 to 904A SIG IN; 904A SIG OUT to 902 (1) SIG IN +; 902 (1) SIG OUT + to OUTPUT L (app); CM1A TRIG (upper) to 911 (1) S-TRIG IN; 911 (1) OUT to 902 (1) CONTROL INPUT 1.
- Listen for: a round, dark bass with a hollow octave under it.

steps.title: A bite on every note
steps.why:
The lower trigger starts the second 911, which goes through CP35 attenuator 1 into the 904A’s CONTROL INPUT 1: about two and a half octaves of sweep.
- 911 (2): T1 0 · 2 ms, T2 4.5 · 92 ms, E SUS 2 · 1.1 V, T3 3 · 26 ms.
- CP35 ATTENUATOR 1 4.
- Cables: CM1A TRIG (lower) to 911 (2) S-TRIG IN; 911 (2) OUT to CP35 IN 1; CP35 OUT 1 to 904A CONTROL INPUT 1.
- Listen for: each note of the gallop clicking open and closing again.

context.cp35.att1: In this sound: how far each note’s filter bite reaches.
context.m921b_3.range: In this sound: the octave the second bank adds below.
context.cp3am_1.gain2: In this sound: the weight of the square underneath.

tweaks.hear: The square joins the saw at pitch: thinner, more hollow.
A brighter, slappier gallop.

sounds.name: Word Up Pulse Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Cameo — “Word Up!”, New York, 1986
sounds.blurb: A tight, nasal pulse bass with a pure sine underneath, snapped short by an exponential amplifier.
sounds.how: A narrow pulse has a reedy, nasal edge that cuts on small speakers, and a sine an octave down puts the weight back. Both 921Bs share the 921A’s width through their LINK WIDTH jacks. No voltage-controlled filter at all: the 923’s gentle low-pass takes the fizz off, and the 902 on EXP turns a plain envelope into a snappy, percussive one.

steps.title: A narrow pulse and a sine below
steps.why:
The first 921A drives both 921Bs, pitch and width. Its WIDTH sets the pulse at about 32 %; the second 921B sits an octave down.
- 921A (1) WIDTH 2.8 · 32 %.
- 921B (1) RANGE 8’.
- 921B (2) RANGE 16’.
- 921 COARSE RNG SUB: the 921 plays no part in this sound, so it goes back to its LFO range.
- Cables: CM1A CV 1 to 921A (1) FREQUENCY IN 1; 921A (1) FREQUENCY TO 921B to 921B (1) LINK FREQ; 921B (1) LINK FREQ (to next) to 921B (2) LINK FREQ; 921A (1) WIDTH TO 921B to 921B (1) LINK WIDTH; 921B (1) LINK WIDTH (to next) to 921B (2) LINK WIDTH.
- Unplug (Default patch): CM1A CV 1 from 921 FREQUENCY CONTROL INPUT 1; 921 SAWTOOTH from 902 (1) SIG IN +.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the oscillators are not patched out.

steps.title: Mix, and soften with the 923
steps.why:
The pulse and the sine into the first CP3A-M, then the 923’s LOW PASS IN, a fixed 6 dB filter that just rounds the top.
- CP3A-M (1): GAIN 1 5, GAIN 2 6, MASTER GAIN 8.
- 923 LOW PASS 7 · 1.3 kHz.
- Cables: 921B (1) RECTANGULAR to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 1; 921B (2) SINE to CP3A-M (1) INPUT 2; CP3A-M (1) OUTPUT + 1 to 923 LOW PASS IN.
- Listen for: a reedy tone over a smooth low end.

steps.title: A snappy exponential amplifier
steps.why:
The 923 into the first 902, set to EXP so the gain falls away quickly after the attack.
- 902 (1) CONTROL MODE EXP.
- 911 (1): T1 0 · 2 ms, T2 5.5 · 220 ms, E SUS 5 · 2.8 V, T3 2.5 · 17 ms.
- Cables: 923 LOW PASS OUT to 902 (1) SIG IN +; 902 (1) SIG OUT + to OUTPUT L (app); CM1A TRIG (upper) to 911 (1) S-TRIG IN; 911 (1) OUT to 902 (1) CONTROL INPUT 1.
- Listen for: short, punchy notes that leave the gaps in the riff open.

context.m921a_1.width: In this sound: how nasal the pulse is.
context.m902_1.mode: In this sound: EXP makes the envelope feel snappier.
context.m923.lp: In this sound: rounds off the top of the pulse.

tweaks.hear: A hollow square: softer, more like a tuba.
Fatter, longer notes that run into each other.

sounds.name: Four-Saw Reese
sounds.ref: In the style of Dillinja — London drum & bass, mid-1990s
sounds.blurb: Four sawtooths, two at pitch and two an octave down, each pair slightly out of tune, churning through a dark ladder.
sounds.how: The Reese bass is detuning made into a sound: two sawtooths a fraction apart beat against each other, and the beating is the movement. With two banks there are four, and each pair beats at its own rate, so the churn never repeats exactly. The keyboard reaches both 921As through the first CP3A-M’s MULTIPLE A.

steps.title: Two banks from one multiple
steps.why:
CM1A CV 1 into CP3A-M (1) MULTIPLE A; two copies to the two 921As. Bank 1 at 8’, its second 921B a little sharp; bank 2 at 16’, its second a little flat.
- 921B (2) FREQUENCY 0.2 · +0.2 st.
- 921B (3) RANGE 16’.
- 921B (4): RANGE 16’, FREQUENCY −0.1 · -0.1 st.
- 921 COARSE RNG SUB: the 921 plays no part in this sound, so it goes back to its LFO range.

sounds.name: Switched Acid Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Ceephax Acid Crew — London acid, 2000s
sounds.blurb: A single sawtooth squelching through a ringing ladder, its cutoff built from three voltages the 992 adds together.
sounds.how: The 992 is a control-voltage mixer made for the filter: three switched inputs and an EXT INPUT with an attenuator that can turn the voltage upside down. Here it adds key tracking from CM1A CV 2, a slow sweep from the 921’s AUX OUT and the second 911 at a set amount, all into one 904A input. Flick a rocker and that part of the movement drops out without touching a cable.

sounds.name: Minneapolis Sync Bass

sounds.name: Five-Oscillator Wall
sounds.ref: In the style of Mike Dean — Houston hip-hop production, 2010s
sounds.blurb: Every oscillator on the System 35 on one note: four sawtooths across two banks and the 921’s square below, a slow, enormous bass.

sounds.name: Filter-Bank House Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Todd Terry — New York house, late 1980s
sounds.blurb: A round, organ-like offbeat house bass, its tone shaped by fixed bands of the 914 rather than a sweeping filter.
sounds.how: The 914 is fourteen fixed filters side by side, each with its own level. Turned up at the bottom and down towards the top, it acts like a fixed tone control that leaves the body of a square and sine bass and takes away its buzz, so every note has the same rounded, organ-like colour, whatever its pitch.

sounds.blurb: A snarling, metallic drum & bass growl: the 921 shaking the ladder’s cutoff at audio rate, and a 921B slowly wobbling it.

sounds.name: Shimmering Alien Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Ben Salisbury & Geoff Barrow — “Annihilation”, 2018
sounds.blurb: A slow, eerie lead whose tone glitters and wobbles, one bank frequency-modulating the other a tritone away.

sounds.name: Three-Rate Beating Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Phill Niblock — the “Touch” drone records, New York, 2000s
sounds.blurb: Four near-unison sine and triangle tones on one held note, beating against each other at three different slow rates that themselves drift.
sounds.how: Both 921A drivers take the keyboard, and each 921B is set a few cents from the others with its FREQUENCY knob, so every pair beats at its own rate: the sound pulses in slow, overlapping waves with no LFO on the level at all. A slow 921 triangle, turned right down in a CP35 attenuator, nudges one oscillator’s pitch so even the beat rates speed up and slow down, the shifting beat patterns Niblock builds from many slightly detuned tones.

sounds.blurb: A warm, muffled drone of open fifths, swelling up and sinking back like a slowed-down tape of brass and strings.

sounds.name: Cancelling Saws Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Deathprod — “Morals and Dogma”, Tromsø, 2004
sounds.blurb: A dark, hollow drone that slowly empties and fills, as two almost-identical saws cancel each other out.
sounds.how: A 902 has an inverting input: what goes into SIG IN − comes out upside down, added to SIG IN +. sounds.name: Half-Wave Time Machine
sounds.ref: In the style of Coil — “Time Machines”, London, 1998
sounds.blurb: A hypnotic, clangorous drone: a sine chord chopped by another oscillator into new, inharmonic tones that slowly shift.

sounds.blurb: A warm, open jazz chord stacked in fourths, every key a whole voicing, gliding in the slow light of a moving filter.

sounds.name: Change-Ringing Tower Bells

sounds.name: Index-Envelope FM Bell
sounds.ref: In the style of Ryuichi Sakamoto — “Merry Christmas Mr. Lawrence”, 1983
sounds.blurb: A glassy, bell-like melody: each note strikes bright and metallic, then mellows to a pure tone.
sounds.how: The second 921B, tuned three and a half times the first’s pitch, frequency-modulates it through its AC MOD. But first it passes through the second 902, opened by a decaying 911: a modulation VCA. sounds.name: Stack-FM Gong

sounds.name: Steam Train Chuff
sounds.ref: In the style of Pierre Schaeffer — “Étude aux chemins de fer”, Paris, 1948
sounds.blurb: A steam engine pulling away: slow chuffs of steam that speed up into a steady rhythm over a low rumble.
sounds.how: Each chuff is a burst of noise that dies away, made by the 921’s falling ramp (the inverted sawtooth on its AUX OUT) in the second 902’s control input: the gain jumps up and slides down every cycle, and the 902 shuts on the negative half. The CM1A’s lower TRIG restarts the ramp at the 921’s TRIG S so the train always starts on a chuff, and the second 911, rising over four seconds, speeds the 921 up as the engine gets going.

sounds.name: Stack-on-Stack FM
sounds.ref: In the style of Iannis Xenakis — “Bohor”, 1962
sounds.blurb: Scattered metallic clangs, each struck hard and mellowing as it rings, in wide leaps across the keyboard.
sounds.how: The whole second stack frequency-modulates the whole first stack at audio rate. Its two 921Bs, tuned to awkward ratios, are mixed in the second CP3A-M and go through the second 902, where the second 911 sets the depth; then through a CP35 attenuator into the first 921A’s FREQUENCY IN 2, so both oscillators of the first stack are modulated together. Because the driver’s input is DC coupled the FM also bends the pitch a little, which adds to the clang.

sounds.name: Cross-Bank Sync Duet
sounds.ref: In the style of Richard Teitelbaum — Musica Elettronica Viva, “Spacecraft”, 1967
sounds.blurb: Two tearing, vocal voices tangled together: one sweeps its timbre while the other glides in pitch.
sounds.how: Each stack syncs the other. The first 921B is hard-synced to the third (the second stack), so it keeps the third’s pitch and its own tuning becomes timbre; the fourth is synced to the second (the first stack). The second 911 sweeps the first stack up: the first 921B tears through its harmonics at the keyboard pitch, while the second 921B rises and drags the fourth’s pitch up with it. One envelope, two quite different results.

sounds.name: Filter-Oscillator Drift
sounds.ref: In the style of Pauline Oliveros — “Bye Bye Butterfly”, 1965
sounds.blurb: A pure tone with nothing feeding it, its timbre shimmering and drifting as an audio-rate wobble moves it.
sounds.how: No oscillator is heard. The 904A, at full REGENERATION, rings on its own as a sine, and CM1A CV 2 tunes it from the keyboard. The 921 on AUDIO, an octave below the note, sends its sine at a low AUX OUT LEVEL into the 904A’s cutoff: audio-rate FM of the filter itself, which gives the tone sidebands. An unlinked 921B on LO slowly detunes the 921 so the sidebands drift.

sounds.name: Self-FM Feedback Loop
sounds.ref: In the style of David Tudor — “Toneburst”, 1975
sounds.blurb: A held tone that grows rougher and wilder as it feeds back on itself, breaking into squealing chaos.
sounds.how: A loop: the first 921B’s sawtooth goes into the 904A, the 904A into the first CP3A-M’s MULTIPLE A, and one copy goes through the second 902 straight back into the same 921B’s AC MOD. The oscillator is modulating itself with its own filtered sound. The second 911 opens that 902 slowly, so the feedback grows through the note, and an LFO moves the 904A’s cutoff, which changes the loop and makes it lurch between states.

sounds.name: Summed-LFO Stepped Melody
sounds.ref: In the style of Ruth White — “Flowers of Evil”, 1969
sounds.blurb: A plucky, slightly eerie line whose notes jump between octaves and tritones in a pattern that never quite repeats.
sounds.how: Three square LFOs at unrelated rates, each in its own input of the second CP3A-M, add up to a stepped voltage: every time one of them flips, the sum jumps. The gains are chosen as intervals: GAIN 1 at 1 makes the 921’s square jump an octave, GAIN 2 at 0.5 makes the third 921B’s jump a tritone, and GAIN 3 at 0.2 gives a small, wonky step. The sum moves the first 921A’s pitch on top of the keyboard, a sample-and-hold-like melody with no sample-and-hold.

sounds.name: Six-Source Summing Machine
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernard Parmegiani — “De Natura Sonorum”, 1975
sounds.blurb: A resonant, restless tone that blips, wobbles and wah-wahs, each note shaped by a different mix of movements.
sounds.how: The 992 and the first CP3A-O are summing switchers: each adds up to three control voltages plus an EXT INPUT through an attenuator, and a rocker takes each one in or out. sounds.name: Audio-Rate 902 Modulation
sounds.ref: In the style of Karlheinz Stockhausen — “Mixtur”, 1964
sounds.blurb: Clangorous, bell-like tones whose overtones are sums and differences of two unrelated pitches.
sounds.how: A 902 is a multiplier: its control inputs are DC coupled and fast, so a sine there at audio rate multiplies the signal and makes new frequencies, the sum and difference of the two. The first stack’s sine is the signal; the second stack’s two sines, at odd ratios, go to the second 902’s CONTROL INPUTs. Because the 902 shuts at 0 V it clips the modulation’s lower half, which adds still more partials. A decaying envelope makes them ring like bells.
